pipelines-flush-backpressure.title: Treat PipeWriter flushes as backpressure boundaries
pipelines-flush-backpressure.short: A flush can asynchronously wait for the reader
pipelines-flush-backpressure.summary: System.IO.Pipelines coordinates producers and consumers; FlushAsync is where a writer can observe completion, cancellation, and pressure from buffered data.
pipelines-flush-backpressure.why: Ignoring the asynchronous flush boundary can let a producer outrun its consumer or mishandle shutdown.
pipelines-flush-backpressure.tips: Await flushes, inspect completion when appropriate, and keep writer ownership clear through shutdown.

socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.title: Understand dual-mode sockets for IPv4 and IPv6
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.short: One IPv6 socket can also serve IPv4 when configured
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.summary: A dual-mode IPv6 socket can reduce duplicated listener logic while still serving IPv4 clients on supported platforms.
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.why: Assuming address-family behavior is identical everywhere can cause listeners or endpoint comparisons to fail unexpectedly.
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.tips: Choose dual-mode behavior deliberately, test deployment platforms, and normalize endpoint handling where representation matters.

dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.title: Avoid temporary keys with compatible dictionary alternate lookup
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.short: Query another key representation without materializing an object
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.summary: Alternate lookup can let compatible key representations participate in dictionary lookup without first allocating a temporary key.
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.why: Creating a short-lived string for every lookup can dominate allocation in parsing-heavy hot paths.
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.tips: Use it only with a compatible comparer and when measurement shows temporary key creation matters.

xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.title: Stream large XML with explicit untrusted-input settings
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.short: Avoid full-document materialization and unwanted external resolution
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.summary: XmlReader provides forward-only XML processing and explicit settings for DTD and external resource handling.
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.why: Blindly loading large or untrusted XML can create avoidable memory pressure and unsafe external-resource behavior.
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.tips: Disable features you do not need, impose application-level size limits, and process large documents incrementally.

assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-assets.title: Resolve plugin assets with AssemblyDependencyResolver
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-assets.short: Follow the plugin dependency context for managed and native assets
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-assets.summary: AssemblyDependencyResolver maps assembly and unmanaged-library names to assets associated with a plugin component.
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-assets.why: Searching arbitrary directories manually can select incompatible versions and makes native dependency resolution fragile.
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-assets.tips: Pair the resolver with a dedicated AssemblyLoadContext and keep plugin loading policy explicit.

memorymappedfile-view-window-lifetime.title: Keep memory-mapped file views bounded and explicitly owned
memorymappedfile-view-window-lifetime.short: Map only the window needed and dispose its view deterministically
memorymappedfile-view-window-lifetime.summary: Memory-mapped files expose file regions through views whose offset, size, access mode, and lifetime should match the work being performed.
memorymappedfile-view-window-lifetime.why: Keeping oversized views alive can retain address-space and native resources far beyond the useful operation.
memorymappedfile-view-window-lifetime.tips: Use bounded views for working regions, dispose them promptly, and coordinate concurrent writers explicitly.

process-async-output-drain-deadlock.title: Drain redirected process output while waiting asynchronously
process-async-output-drain-deadlock.short: Do not wait for a child process while its output pipe is blocked
process-async-output-drain-deadlock.summary: Redirected stdout and stderr use bounded pipes, so parent and child can deadlock if output is not drained while the child is running.
process-async-output-drain-deadlock.why: Waiting for exit before reading redirected output can leave the child blocked on a full pipe and unable to exit.
process-async-output-drain-deadlock.tips: Start output reads before awaiting process exit and define cancellation and stderr handling deliberately.

regex-source-generation-aot-boundary.title: Use generated regular expressions when startup and AOT constraints matter
regex-source-generation-aot-boundary.short: Move regex construction work to generated code where appropriate
regex-source-generation-aot-boundary.summary: GeneratedRegex can produce regex implementation code at build time, reducing runtime construction work and fitting environments where dynamic code is constrained.
regex-source-generation-aot-boundary.why: Repeated runtime regex construction adds startup and allocation cost, while dynamic compilation may not suit AOT deployment.
regex-source-generation-aot-boundary.tips: Generate stable patterns, keep timeout and input-trust decisions explicit, and benchmark before optimizing ordinary cases.

channel-completion-error-propagation.title: Design Channel completion and producer error propagation together
channel-completion-error-propagation.short: Completion is part of the producer-consumer contract
channel-completion-error-propagation.summary: A Channel can complete normally or with an error, and consumers need a deliberate policy for distinguishing shutdown, cancellation, and producer failure.
channel-completion-error-propagation.why: Treating every end of iteration as successful completion can hide producer faults or turn expected shutdown into noisy errors.
channel-completion-error-propagation.tips: Complete the writer exactly once, propagate meaningful failures, and keep cancellation separate from producer faults where possible.

unity-physics-nonalloc-buffer-sizing.title: Size Unity non-alloc physics buffers with truncation in mind
unity-physics-nonalloc-buffer-sizing.short: Allocation-free queries need an explicit overflow policy
unity-physics-nonalloc-buffer-sizing.summary: Unity non-alloc physics queries write results into caller-owned arrays, avoiding per-call result-array allocation but imposing a fixed capacity.
unity-physics-nonalloc-buffer-sizing.why: A full result buffer can mean the query had more hits than fit, so silently consuming it as complete can create correctness bugs.
unity-physics-nonalloc-buffer-sizing.tips: Choose capacity from measured scenes, detect full buffers, and define retry, growth, or truncation behavior outside hot loops.
